title: Add Argo CI regen-diff check for brand-kit (implements ADR-1)
description:
Implements docs/plan/plan.md ADR-1.

Add an Argo WorkflowTemplate (in jedarden/declarative-config,
k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/, per this workspace's Argo-only CI policy) that,
on push to brand-kit main:
  1. Checks out the repo in a clean container with Pillow + resvg installed.
  2. Runs `python3 tools/trace_logo.py` (if source/logo.png changed) and
     `python3 tools/build_assets.py`.
  3. `git diff --exit-code` against the committed tree; fail the workflow if
     anything differs.

This turns "did you remember to re-run the build script before committing"
into an enforced CI invariant instead of a trust-based README instruction.
No existing CI/WorkflowTemplate covers brand-kit today (confirmed: no
.github/, no template in the CLAUDE.md WorkflowTemplate table).

Acceptance: pushing a change to source/logo.svg without re-running
build_assets.py fails the workflow; pushing a properly-regenerated change
passes.

title: Add explicit LICENSE file (repo currently shows license: null on GitHub)
description:
README.md's "Usage & rights" section states these are personal brand assets,
all rights reserved, not licensed for reuse/redistribution. But the repo has
no LICENSE file — confirmed via `gh api /repos/jedarden/brand-kit` returning
"license": null. GitHub's UI shows public repos with no LICENSE as
ambiguous/unlicensed rather than clearly "all rights reserved," which is a
weaker signal than the README text already asserts.

Concrete change: add a LICENSE file at repo root with a short explicit
"All rights reserved" copyright notice (name + year), consistent with the
README's existing "Usage & rights" wording. No need for a template
open-source license — the point is making the existing restriction visible
via the standard GitHub license-detection path.

title: Add tools/verify_assets.py: check shipped PNG dimensions match README's per-platform table
description:
Nothing currently checks that README.md's per-platform dimension table
(e.g. "avatars/x-400.png (400x400)") actually matches the real pixel
dimensions of the committed file. They happen to all match today (spot
checked 2026-07-20), but there's no guard against the table and the assets
drifting apart independently.

Add tools/verify_assets.py: a small script (Pillow) with a dict of
{path: (expected_w, expected_h)} mirroring the README table, that opens each
file and asserts actual size matches, exiting non-zero on any mismatch. Wire
it into the same CI check as the regen-diff (see "Add Argo CI regen-diff
check for brand-kit", references docs/plan/plan.md ADR-1) so both classes of
drift — source vs. derived, and derived vs. documented — are caught in one
pass.

title: Add transparent-background logo variant for overlay/dark-surface use
description:
Every logo output today (logo/logo-*.png, avatars/*.png, favicon/*) is
flattened to RGB with the Canvas Cream (#EFDECC) background baked in — there
is no alpha channel anywhere (verified 2026-07-20: PIL reports mode "RGB" on
logo/logo-512.png and favicon/favicon-32.png, corner pixel ~(239,221,203)
matching the cream fill). That's fine for square/circle avatar slots
(platform chrome already supplies a background), but there's no way to drop
the logo onto something else — a colored banner, a dark card, a print
layout — without the cream box.

Concrete change: in tools/build_assets.py's logo_at(), keep an
alpha-preserving path (resvg output before the .convert("RGB") flattening
step) and emit at least one new output, e.g. logo/logo-512-transparent.png
(and ideally the same set as logo/logo-*.png), by rendering source/logo.svg
without compositing onto the cream rect. Requires checking whether
source/logo.svg's background is a separate <rect> element that can be
excluded, or whether the SVG needs a variant with no background layer. Add
the new file(s) to the README's "Logo masters" section.

title: Resolve source/hero-alt.png: 2MB, unused by tools/build_assets.py, no documented purpose beyond README's 'kept for reference'
description:
source/hero-alt.png (2.0MB) is never read by tools/build_assets.py (only
source/hero.png and source/logo.svg/logo.png are consumed) or
tools/trace_logo.py. README.md's only mention is: "source/hero-alt.png is an
alternate desk composition kept for reference." That's dead weight in every
clone with no way for a future reader to know if/when it should replace
hero.png, or whether it's safe to delete.

Concrete action (pick one): either (a) add a sentence to README explaining
the actual criteria for promoting hero-alt.png to hero.png / what makes it
worth keeping, or (b) if there's no real plan to use it, remove it from the
repo (git history retains it if ever needed) to cut ~2MB of unused weight.
Either resolution is fine; the point is removing the ambiguous "kept for
reference" non-answer.

title: Optimize PNG output size in tools/build_assets.py (banners/ is 9.8MB, youtube banner alone is 3.1MB)
description:
tools/build_assets.py saves every derived PNG with PIL defaults (Image.save
with no optimize/compression tuning). Measured today: banners/ totals 9.8MB,
with banners/youtube-banner-2560x1440.png alone at 3.1MB. These are meant to
be dropped straight into upload dialogs (per README) — smaller files without
visible quality loss make the kit more pleasant to actually use and
self-host.

Concrete change: in the `save()` helper, either
  - add `img.save(out, optimize=True)` (free, no dependency) and/or
  - shell out to `oxipng -o4 <path>` / `pngquant` as a post-process pass
    (documented as an optional-but-recommended tool in README's "Regenerating"
    section, mirroring the existing resvg/vtracer pattern),
then re-run tools/build_assets.py and commit the smaller output. Verify no
visible quality regression on the banners (photoreal hero crops) — spot-check
a couple at 100% zoom before committing.

title: Tag brand-kit v1.0.0 release once CI regen-check is green (implements ADR-1)
description:
Implements docs/plan/plan.md ADR-1.

Blocked on the Argo regen-diff CI check landing (companion bead: "Add Argo
CI regen-diff check for brand-kit"). Once CI is green on main:
  1. git tag v1.0.0 (current committed asset set is already internally
     consistent as of commit d51a763).
  2. Create a GitHub Release from the tag with brief notes (logo vectorized,
     full per-platform asset set).
  3. Add a one-line CHANGELOG.md (or a "## Releases" section in README.md)
     recording the tag -> commit mapping going forward, so consumers have
     something citable instead of "whatever main was on the day I copied it."

This is the first step toward consumers (starting with jedarden.com) pinning
to a version instead of ad hoc copy-paste; the actual migration of
jedarden.com is out of scope for this repo/bead.

title: Add GitHub repo topics for discoverability (repo currently has zero topics)
description:
`gh api /repos/jedarden/brand-kit` shows "topics": [] — no topics set, so the
repo doesn't surface in GitHub topic search/browse at all despite being
public and reusable-by-reference.

Concrete change: `gh repo edit jedarden/brand-kit --add-topic branding
--add-topic logo --add-topic personal-brand --add-topic social-media-assets
--add-topic svg` (adjust list as fits). One command, no code change. Low
priority polish, cheap to ship.
